thread.title: Stock Market Record Highs; S&P 500 Tops 2900, But Best Buy Crumbles

author: SCOTT LEHTONEN
title: Stock Market Record Highs; S&P 500 Tops 2900, But Best Buy Crumbles
text:
The stock market continued its solid advance early Tuesday with modest gains. Top growth stock Align Technology ( ALGN ) is breaking out above a potential buy point — according to MarketSmith chart analysis — while retailer Best Buy ( BBY ) fell back to its recent buy point after disappointing earnings. ( For updates on this story and other market coverage, visit the Stock Market Today .)
X All three major indexes — the Dow Jones industrial average, the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite and the S&P 500 — moved up about 0.2% apiece. The S&P 500 topped the 2900 price level for the first time.
Among the Dow stocks , Apple ( AAPL ) stock gained nearly 1% to reach a new high. Shares are up nearly 12% from a flat base's 194.30 buy point.
Among companies reporting earnings, hot IPO stock BJ's Wholesale Club ( BJ ) fell 5% after the company reported better-than-expected earnings . Shares hit a record high early Monday only to reverse lower and fall over 6%. The stock also gave up its 27.56 buy point on Monday.

The stock fell below its 78.07 cup-with-handle entry after being up as much as 8% from that level. Best Buy stock is testing its 50-day line.
High-end jeweler Tiffany ( TIF ) pared a 7% surged to 1%, briefly regaining its 50-day line and near a new high after its earnings results topped the Street's estimates. A recent breakout above a flat base's 138.07 buy point failed when it triggered the 7%-8% loss-cutting sell signal.
DSW ( DSW ) soared over 20% to a new high after crushing its Q2 estimates and raising its full-year guidance. The retailer fell below its 50-day line on Aug. 17, but was able to regain that level in the following trading sessions.
Inside The IBD 50 Among the top growth stocks , Align Technology ( ALGN ) is breaking out above a flat base's 385.10 buy point in early trade. The flat base is a later-stage base. Shares moved up over 1%.
On the downside, Control4 ( CTRL ) faltered 6% after analyst firm Imperial Capital downgraded the smart-home stock from outperform to in-line. The stock triggered the round-trip sell signal after giving back the entirety of an over-10% gain from a 33.57 cup-with-handle entry.
